function: Multi-agent DQN picks each VSAT's sensing subcarriers and transmit power in ISAC uplink to a LEO satellite, avoiding sensing collisions under SE and sensing-error QoS; pp. 9-10.
system: Uplink MIMO-OFDM ISAC from VSAT (4x4 UPA) to LEO (8x8 UPA), 8 subcarriers (6 in MADRL test, 3 VSATs), S-band 2 GHz, 100 MHz; no RIS; pp. 11-13.
method: Distributed DQN agents (five fully connected layers, epsilon-greedy), reinforcement learning trained offline with a central global reward, decentralized inference; the beamforming part uses non-learned Riemannian optimization; pp. 9-11.
data_channel: Own simulation: Rician fading, free-space path loss, Starlink orbital geometry; 500 random channel realizations for training, 100 for testing; no 3GPP profile or measured data; pp. 11, 13.
test_conditions: Training on random channel realizations 1-500, testing on held-out realizations 501-600 of the same 3-VSAT, 6-subcarrier scenario; no new scenario or adaptation; p. 13.
baselines: Learned part: distributed ISAC optimization (each VSAT senses on 50% of its own communication subcarriers), non-learned; optimization part: DSAC, TD-SAC, conventional ISAC; no learned baseline; pp. 11, 14.
metrics: Spectral efficiency, sensing beampattern error, collision rate, sum power, reward during training and testing, half-power beamwidth and sidelobe level; pp. 8, 12-14.
complexity: Orders stated: optimization design O(NelNazNs^6+4J2Ntx^2Ns+K1NtxNrx^2); MADRL training O(Emax Imax sum D n_{l-1} n_l); Riemannian solver converges in about 0.1 s per subcarrier; pp. 7, 11.
q1_support: p. 11: "the wireless channel for the NTN is modeled using Rician fading with large-scale fading [1]" - own simulator with free-space path loss; TR 38.811 is cited only to neglect atmospheric loss below 6 GHz, not as the channel model.
q2_support: p. 13: "The first 500 random channel realizations are used during the training phase, while the random channels with indices from 501 to 600 are used for testing" - a held-out part of the same scenario; no other scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 14: "40% higher than that of the distributed ISAC" optimization approach, which is non-learned; the other baselines (DSAC, TD-SAC, conventional ISAC, p. 11) are non-learned too; no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "computational complexity to train the proposed MADRL-ISAC algorithm is given by" an order in Emax, Imax, batch size and layer widths; p. 7 gives the order of the optimization design.
q5_support: p. 11: "The LEO satellite network is modeled in MATLAB using the satelliteScenario object" - simulated channels, Starlink orbital parameters [34] set only the geometry; no code or data link is given.
notes: The main design is optimization (Riemannian manifold, SVD), included because Section VI adds a learned MADRL-ISAC (DQN) that selects sensing subcarriers and power in a satellite link; area 6 by the tie-break order (satellite link that also senses). Handover itself is above the physical layer, but the learned decisions are subcarriers and power. The imperfect-CSI study (Section VII-D) concerns the optimization design, not the learned model. TR 38.811 [36] is cited only for negligible atmospheric loss below 6 GHz. Tables II and III and Figs. 7, 18 and 19 were read as page images.
